title: The 5 Tallest Waterfalls on Earth, Ranked (Niagara Isn't Close)

scenes.text: The five tallest waterfalls on Earth. Niagara doesn't come close to making the list.

scenes.label: Yumbilla · 896 m
scenes.text: Number five: Yumbilla Falls in Peru. Eight hundred ninety-six meters, nearly three thousand feet of falling water.

scenes.label: Olo'upena · 900 m
scenes.text: Number four: Olo'upena Falls in Hawaii. About nine hundred meters, close to three thousand feet.

scenes.label: Tres Hermanas · 914 m
scenes.text: Number three: Tres Hermanas Falls in Peru. Its name means Three Sisters, and it drops nine hundred fourteen meters.

scenes.label: Tugela · 947 m
scenes.text: Number two: Tugela Falls in South Africa. About nine hundred forty-seven meters, and some people say it deserves first place.

scenes.label: Angel Falls · 979 m
scenes.text: Number one: Angel Falls in Venezuela. Nine hundred seventy-nine meters, almost three Eiffel Towers stacked on top of each other.

description:
The five tallest waterfalls on Earth by overall height, ranked.
Angel Falls in Venezuela drops 979 meters, though people still argue about how to measure a waterfall.
Which of these would you want to see in person?
first_comment: Which waterfall would you travel to see? And what should we rank next?
